title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time around Carleton, with access limits noted.

cards.title: Hike the Cowling Arboretum trails
cards.subtitle: Cowling Arboretum, adjacent to campus
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a trail walk and stay on marked routes; check the visitor rules before heading into either section of the Arb.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission walk through Carleton’s roughly 800-acre Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton states that the Cowling Arboretum is open to public use year-round and has an extensive trail system.
cards.access_notes: Open to public use year-round; follow Arboretum visitor rules.

cards.title: Run the Arb trail system
cards.subtitle: Cowling Arboretum, adjacent to campus
cards.notes: Use the trail map to choose a comfortable loop, yield thoughtfully, and keep the outing social by setting a regroup point before starting.
cards.short_summary: A trail-running hang on the Arb’s public-use paths.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton identifies the Arboretum as year-round public-use land and describes its trail system as suitable for running.
cards.access_notes: Open to public use year-round; use designated trails.

cards.title: Ride designated Upper Arb trails
cards.subtitle: Upper Cowling Arboretum, south of Highway 19
cards.notes: Bring a bike and follow the map’s designated routes only; the visitor rules prohibit cycling in the Lower Arboretum.
cards.short_summary: A bring-your-own-bike outing on the Arb’s permitted Upper Arb routes.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Arboretum trail map says visitors enjoy limited biking and permits bikes only on specifically designated Upper Arboretum trails.
cards.source_title: Cowling Arboretum Trail Map and Rules for Visitors
cards.access_notes: Bring your own bike; cycling is allowed only on designated Upper Arb trails.

cards.title: Take a Lower Arb nature walk
cards.subtitle: Lower Cowling Arboretum, north of Highway 19
cards.notes: Walk the lower trails for a quieter nature-focused outing, keeping to the route and respecting seasonal deer-hunt restrictions.
cards.short_summary: A public trail walk through the Arb’s lower, floodplain section.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s visitor map welcomes visitors, describes Lower Arb trails and states that public use during the deer archery hunt is restricted to trails.
cards.source_title: Cowling Arboretum Trail Map and Rules for Visitors
cards.access_notes: Use trails only; during the deer archery hunt, public use is restricted to trails.

cards.title: See a Weitz Center exhibit
cards.subtitle: Weitz Center for Creativity, Carleton campus
cards.notes: Check the current arts calendar, then meet in the building’s exhibition areas and take time to compare what each person notices.
cards.short_summary: An exhibit-focused visit in Carleton’s arts center.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton states that most exhibits at the Weitz Center are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Most exhibits are free and open to the public; confirm the individual listing before visiting.

cards.title: Catch a free Weitz performance
cards.subtitle: Weitz Center for Creativity, Carleton campus
cards.notes: Choose a listed performance with free admission, arrive a little early, and use the lobby as a low-key pre-show meetup spot.
cards.short_summary: A performance outing in Carleton’s arts center when the listed show is free.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton states that most performances in Weitz Center spaces are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Most performances are free and open to the public; verify admission on the specific event listing.

cards.title: Go to a free Weitz film screening
cards.subtitle: Weitz Center for Creativity, Carleton campus
cards.notes: Find a screening marked free on the arts calendar and make it a shared movie night without needing to buy a ticket.
cards.short_summary: A cinema outing at Weitz when the screening is listed as free.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton states that most movie screenings in Weitz Center spaces are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Most movie screenings are free and open to the public; verify the individual screening’s admission details.

cards.title: Attend a Carleton Convocation
cards.subtitle: Carleton College Chapel
cards.notes: Look for the next speaker on the college calendar and invite a classmate to discuss one idea from the talk after it ends.
cards.short_summary: A speaker event presented at Carleton’s Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus-tour material describes Convocation as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public according to Carleton’s tour material; confirm the current schedule and venue.

cards.entity_name: Carleton student theater and dance performances
cards.title: See a student performance
cards.subtitle: Weitz Center for Creativity, Carleton campus
cards.notes: Check the performance calendar for a student-produced theater or dance show, then plan around the listed venue and start time.
cards.short_summary: A no-ticket student arts outing when the show is listed as free.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus-tour material says student theater and dance performances occur regularly and are free.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current arts calendar for a scheduled student performance and venue details.

cards.entity_name: Carleton Association of Nature and Outdoor Enthusiasts equipment lending
cards.title: Borrow outdoor gear through CANOE
cards.subtitle: Carleton College, Northfield
cards.notes: Ask CANOE about available equipment and borrowing steps, then pair the gear with a permitted outdoor plan such as an Arb walk.
cards.short_summary: A student outdoor-gear lending option documented as free of charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s climate action plan states that CANOE lends outdoor equipment for independent student use free of charge.
cards.access_notes: For Carleton students; contact CANOE to confirm current inventory and borrowing procedures.

warnings: Several official pages establish that eligible offerings are free but do not replace checking the current event calendar, seasonal rules, or student-organization procedures before going.
